title: Spring Floral Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with a hint of lavender, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake, topped with real edible flowers.
description: These cupcakes taste like a garden party in cake form. I tested this batch three times in my kitchen to get the lavender just right, not soapy, just soft and floral. The base is a simple vanilla bean cupcake with a touch of sour cream for moisture. A quick vanilla buttercream and a scatter of edible rose, pansy, and lavender make it feel special without extra work.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vanilla bean paste (or pure vanilla extract)
1/2 tsp culinary lavender buds, finely ground
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
Edible rose petals, pansy flowers, and lavender buds, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, salt, and ground lavender in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla bean paste.
Add flour mixture in three parts, alternating with milk and sour cream. Mix just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat frosting butter until pale, then add powdered sugar in batches with cream and vanilla. Beat until smooth and pipeable.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe frosting high in a swirl. Top with fresh rose petals, pansies, and a few lavender buds.
tips: Use culinary grade lavender only. Garden lavender can taste bitter or soapy.
Buy edible flowers from a food supplier, not a florist. Florist flowers may have pesticides.
Add flowers right before serving so petals stay fresh and bright.
If your kitchen is warm, chill the frosted cupcakes 10 minutes before adding delicate petals.

faq.question: Where do I find edible flowers for these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Look for edible flowers at farmers markets, specialty grocery stores, or online spice shops that sell culinary lavender. Always confirm the seller labels them food safe.

faq.question: Can I skip the lavender in the batter and just use it as garnish?
faq.answer: Yes, you can leave lavender out of the batter and only use dried buds on top. The cupcake will taste like plain vanilla with a floral finish.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes for a spring party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store unfrosted in an airtight container. Frost and add flowers the same day you serve them.

faq.question: Why does my lavender taste bitter instead of floral?
faq.answer: Bitterness usually means too much lavender or buds that are not culinary grade. Start with 1/2 teaspoon and grind it fine before adding to the flour.

conclusion: These floral cupcakes are a simple way to bring spring to the table. Bake them for a bridal shower, Easter brunch, or just a Sunday treat with tea.
